provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Welcome back songs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing the welcome song
The pupils should be able to add new claps

Introduction:
We are back in school today.
Let us sing our welcome song.

Content:
Sing the class welcome song.
Add new claps to the song.
Practice the song with actions.

Class activity:
Children stand in a circle and sing.
They add claps after each line.

Evaluation questions:
What is our class welcome song?
Show me how to clap.
Can you sing the song?

Summary:
We sang our welcome song with claps.

topics.title: One two three four five
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count to five
The pupils should be able to do the catch the fish action

Introduction:
We can count with our fingers.
Today we learn a counting rhyme.

Content:
Recite one two three four five.
Count on fingers as we recite.
Add catch the fish action.

Class activity:
Children count on fingers.
They pretend to catch fish.

Evaluation questions:
What comes after three?
Show me how to catch a fish.
Can you count to five?

Summary:
We counted to five with actions.

topics.title: Five little ducks
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count down from five
The pupils should be able to do the waddling song

Introduction:
We know how to count up.
Today we count down with ducks.

Content:
Use duck puppets to count down.
Sing the five little ducks song.
Add waddling actions.

Class activity:
Children waddle like ducks.
They count down with puppets.

Evaluation questions:
How many ducks went away?
Show me how to waddle.
What sound does a duck make?

Summary:
We counted down with duck actions.

topics.title: The farmer in the dell
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to act the farmer and the cheese
The pupils should be able to play the circle game

Introduction:
We know about farms and animals.
Today we play a farmer game.

Content:
Recite the farmer in the dell rhyme.
Act the farmer taking a wife.
Play the circle game passing the cheese.

Class activity:
Children form a circle.
They pass a toy cheese around.

Evaluation questions:
What does the farmer do?
Show me how to pass the cheese.
Who is in the dell?

Summary:
We played the farmer circle game.

topics.title: Head and shoulders
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to touch body parts
The pupils should be able to do the speed round

Introduction:
We know our body parts.
Today we sing about them.

Content:
Recite head and shoulders knees and toes.
Touch each part as we sing.
Do a speed round singing fast.

Class activity:
Children touch body parts while singing.
They try to sing very fast.

Evaluation questions:
What body parts do we sing about?
Show me how to touch your knees.
Can you sing fast?

Summary:
We touched body parts while singing.

topics.title: Bingo
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to clap the missing letters
The pupils should be able to spell Bingo together

Introduction:
We know our letters.
Today we spell a special word.

Content:
Recite the Bingo song.
Clap the missing letters instead.
Spell B-I-N-G-O together.

Class activity:
Children clap instead of letters.
They spell Bingo with claps.

Evaluation questions:
What word do we spell?
Show me how to clap a letter.
Can you spell Bingo?

Summary:
We clapped the missing letters.

topics.title: I'm a little teapot
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite with teapot actions
The pupils should be able to do the pouring action song

Introduction:
We know about teapots.
Today we sing a teapot song.

Content:
Recite I'm a little teapot.
Do teapot actions while reciting.
Add pouring actions to the song.

Class activity:
Children pretend to be teapots.
They pour imaginary tea.

Evaluation questions:
What does a teapot do?
Show me how to pour tea.
Can you be a teapot?

Summary:
We did teapot actions while singing.

topics.title: Two little dickie birds
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to act Peter and Paul with fingers
The pupils should be able to fly the birds away and back

Introduction:\{We know about birds.
Today we sing about two birds.

Content:
Recite two little dickie birds.
Act Peter and Paul with fingers.
Fly the birds away and back.

Class activity:
Children use fingers for birds.
They fly fingers away and back.

Evaluation questions:
What are the birds' names?
Show me how to fly a bird.
Can you make bird sounds?

Summary:
We flew our finger birds.

topics.title: Hot cross buns
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite and clap the rhythm
The pupils should be able to sing one a penny, two a penny

Introduction:
We know about buns from the market.
Today we sing about hot cross buns.

Content:
Recite hot cross buns.
Clap the rhythm as we recite.
Sing one a penny, two a penny.

Class activity:
Children clap the rhythm.
They pretend to sell buns.

Evaluation questions:
What are hot cross buns?
Show me how to clap the rhythm.
How much is a bun?

Summary:
We clapped the bun rhythm.

topics.title: Rhyme concert
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to pick and sing rhymes
The pupils should be able to clap for every group

Introduction:
We have learned many rhymes.
Today we have a concert.

Content:
Groups pick a rhyme to sing.
Each group performs their rhyme.
Children clap for every group.

Class activity:
Children form groups.
Each group sings a rhyme.
Others clap after each performance.

Evaluation questions:
Which rhyme did your group sing?
Show how to clap for performers.
Can you name all rhymes?

Summary:
We had a rhyme concert.
